# Crosscheck studies

> Crosscheck checks what an AI coding agent claims about code with proofs, tests and reproductions, and counts only deterministic checks and human decisions as evidence. Each study shows its evidence and its limits.

Every page is plain HTML that reads in full without script. Each study marks its evidence as Proved, Tested, Decided by Harry, Assumed or Not yet reached, and only deterministic checks and human decisions count as evidence.

## EVerest and OCPP 1.6: a formal study

> EVerest restarts a daily charging schedule one second early. Each question shows a short answer and the evidence for it, marked as proved, tested, decided by Harry, assumed or not yet reached.

Work in progress. These are the study's reported results, and this website did not rerun them. This page summarizes evidence from the linked study. It is not an evidence-record/1 file, an automatic attestation, a new run of the experiment, or a fresh check of the proofs.

What the evidence says, by strength:

- Proved: Three rules of the reference model. Lean checks the proofs. About the Lean model, not a proof about EVerest's code.
- Tested: Schedules anchored in 2017–2025. 2,000 generated cases. All 2,000 pass. At the 57,304 moments where the model gives a limit, the two agree within tolerance. At the other 10,226 moments, neither gives a limit.
- Tested: Schedules anchored in 2010–2016. 2,000 generated cases. 835 pass, 92 warn and 1,073 fail, as the study reported. The report also counts 1,081 moments where only EVerest gives a limit; see the caveat on how those are classified.
- Not yet reached: A fourth model rule. Stated without a completed proof. No proof claimed.

EVerest issue #3323 reports the finding upstream. It was filed on 2026-10-29 and is open. This website does not file or update upstream issues.

By 2026-11-10: 19 with a merged fix, 8 with a fix open, 1 with neither; 16 closed by the maintainers.

- [Crosscheck: studies of checked code](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/): Crosscheck checks what an AI coding agent claims about code with proofs, tests and reproductions, and counts only deterministic checks and human decisions as evidence. Each study shows its evidence and its limits.
- [EVerest and OCPP 1.6: a formal study](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/): EVerest restarts a daily charging schedule one second early. Each question shows a short answer and the evidence for it, marked as proved, tested, decided by Harry, assumed or not yet reached.
- [Glossary: EVerest and OCPP 1.6: a formal study](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html): Plain-English explanations of the specialist terms used on the Crosscheck site.

## Glossary of the EVerest study

- [EVerest](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#everest): Open-source software for running an electric-vehicle charging station, maintained as a Linux Foundation Energy project. This study tested its code for combining charging schedules.
- [OCPP](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#ocpp): Open Charge Point Protocol: shared rules for communication between electric-vehicle charging stations and the software managing them. This study checks charging schedules under version 1.6.
- [Schedule anchor](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#schedule-anchor): The moment a schedule first started. A daily schedule restarts at that time of day. The study groups its test cases by the year of the anchor.
- [Leap second](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#leap-second): An extra second sometimes added to clock time to keep it in line with Earth’s rotation.
- [Reference model](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#reference-program): A program describing the behavior we expect. We compare its answers with the code being checked. It covers only the behavior it describes.
- [Lean](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#lean): A language for precisely describing how code should behave, and a tool for checking mathematical arguments about those descriptions.
- [Proof](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#proof): A computer-checked mathematical argument that a rule always holds under stated assumptions. It does not tell us whether the rule is the right one.
- [Differential testing](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#differential-testing): Run the same chosen inputs through two programs and compare their answers. A difference needs investigation. Matching answers cover only the inputs tried.
- [Tolerance](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#tolerance): How close two limits must be to count as agreeing: within 0.05 of the profile’s unit, amps (A) or watts (W).
- [Vacuous pass](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#vacuous-pass): A passing case where the reference model gives no limit at any instant compared, so there was nothing to agree with.
- [Trusted base](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#trusted-base): The parts assumed to work correctly for a result to hold, such as the program checking the proof and the program running the tests.
- [Signed reading](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#signed-reading): The interpretation of the standard that Harry approved in the signed spec. Where the standard’s wording allows more than one reading, the study follows this one.
- [Correspondence review](https://crosscheck.harrynicholls.com/studies/everest-ocpp/glossary.html#correspondence-review): An AI review that searched for mismatches between the model and the written rules. Its findings needed Harry’s decision and do not count as evidence.
